content: The bronchus is approximately 5 cm in length and enters the right lung near the level of the fifth thoracic vertebra. The azygos vein arches over the bronchus from behind, while the right pulmonary artery is initially positioned below it and then moves to lie in front of it. At a distance of about 2 cm from its origin, the bronchus gives rise to a branch that supplies the upper lobe of the right lung. This branch is referred to as the eparterial branch of the bronchus because it originates above the right pulmonary artery. Subsequently, the bronchus passes below the pulmonary artery and is then termed the hyparterial branch. It further divides into two branches, which supply the middle and lower lobes of the right lung.
